To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a synthetic carbohydrate inhibitor of selectin-mediated leukocyte-endothelial adhesion attenuated the lung injury associated with septic shock in pigs.
a synthetic sialyated oligosacchride, CY-15003, attenuated sepsis-induced neutrophil activation and lung injury.
CY-1503 treatment attenuated sepsis-induced pulmonary inflammation and injury, but did not alter the sepsis-induced neutrophil activation or systemic hemodynamic derangments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of carbohydrate-protein interactions in septic shock-induced lung injury.
the role of selectins in neutrophil recruitment to sites of inflammation, and the potential of blocking this recruitment with a novel sialylated synthetic oligosaccharidic ligand.
the development and application of novel carbohydrate-based therapeutics for the treatment of sepsis and septic shock.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CY-1503 is not effective for the prevention and treatment of sepsis-induced pulmonary injury.
CY-1503 treatment attenuated sepsis-induced pulmonary hypertension, hypotension, and lung injury.
sialyl Lewis-X analogs, CY-1502 and CY-1505, have a protective effect in sepsis, but the mechanism is unknown.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the administration of the sialyl Lewis-X analog CY-1503 attenuated the development of acute lung injury during sepsis, despite neutropenia and persistent neutrophil activation.
CY-1503 treatment of septic pigs attenuates acute lung injury by reducing the influx of activated neutrophils into the lung.
the administration of CY-1505, a sialyl Lewis x analogue, attenuated sepsis-induced neutrophil-mediated lung injury in pigs, despite the fact that neutrophil activation was not prevented.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated that sialylated carbohydrate ligands can attenuate sepsis-induced pulmonary injury, and this may have therapeutic implications.
we have shown that the synthetic sialyl oligosaccharides are effective in reducing lung injury and neutrophil activation.
the use of sialyl Lewis-X analogs may have a therapeutic benefit in sepsis.
